title: Conditionals
summary: Make decisions with if, else if, else and switch, and understand truthy and falsy values.

quiz.explain: The first condition is false, so JavaScript tries the next one. `65 >= 60` is true, so it prints `B` and skips the rest.

quiz.q: Which of these values is falsy?
quiz.explain: The common falsy values are `false`, `0`, `''` (empty string), `null`, `undefined` and `NaN`. The text `'0'` and an empty array are truthy.

quiz.q: Click the line that is wrong. The program should print Adult only when age is 18 or more, but it prints Adult for age 15.
quiz.explain: A single `=` assigns instead of comparing. Write `age >= 18` (or `age === 18`) in the condition.

quiz.q: What does this program print? Write the two lines separated by a space.
quiz.explain: The `sat` case has no `break`, so execution falls through into the next case. Always end each case with `break` unless you want this.

quiz.q: Put the lines in order to build a complete if / else.
quiz.explain: The condition and opening brace come first, then the block for true, then `else`, then the block for false, and finally the closing brace.

exercise.task:
In `conditionals.js`, write and export three functions:

- `grade(marks)` returns `'A'` for 80 or more, `'B'` for 60 or more, `'C'` for 40 or more, otherwise `'F'`.
- `dayType(day)` uses a `switch` and returns `'weekend'` for `'saturday'` and `'sunday'`, and `'weekday'` for anything else.
- `displayName(name)` returns `name` if it has a value, or `'Guest'` when `name` is falsy (empty text, `null`, `undefined`).
hints: grade needs a chain of conditions checked from the highest limit down. dayType needs a switch with two cases sharing one result.
Stack `case 'saturday':` and `case 'sunday':` above one `return 'weekend';`. For displayName, `if (name)` is true only for truthy values.
